  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)

Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires the owning Payroll Specialist role, which E023 does not hold. Requested write is at the allowed maximum. Recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent, note 5 by Facilities agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check for E023 (Kathryn Bishop): record shows contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with earlier notes claiming full-time). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Kathryn has basic training, so her maximum access is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum; recommend read.
reason: Conflicting employment-type records: HR's note says full_time, but the Security agent's own database check shows E023 (Kathryn Bishop) is a contractor with only basic security training and explicitly flags the conflict.
